title: Agent-to-Agent Attack Chain (Orchestrator identity spoofing)
summary: As documented, a spoofed agent identity makes two agents perform actions that neither should allow alone. As implemented, the effect is an acceptance reply.

LC.rationale: In the default simulated configuration the A2A handler returns a fixed scripted reply and no model is called, so attacker-supplied natural language does not reach any privileged decision or tool-invocation path.

CP.rationale: The A2A handler answers only the latest message and the lab profile states there is no cross-session persistence outside MemoryBot, which is not on this path.

AP.rationale: The handler sends no message to the Worker and the Worker runs nothing, so the effect is confined to the initially affected Orchestrator endpoint.

RH.rationale: No evaluator, verifier or reward channel is reachable on this path; the handler only returns a scripted acceptance reply and no proxy objective exists.

ES.rationale: No dynamic or unvetted extension is invoked on the assessed path; the A2A handler is a fixed scripted reply with no tool binding.

agentic_applicability.rationale: The lab documents the Orchestrator as trusting the self-declared identity, delegating a dangerous task, and the Worker executing it, which models goal pursuit and action sequencing across agents.
